title: Adic descent of compatible formal ideal thickenings
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian semilocal ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with Jacobson radical $\mathfrak r$ the intersection of its finitely many maximal ideals. Let $J\subseteq\mathfrak r$ and $C=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak r^n$. For each nonmaximal prime $\mathfrak Q\subset C$ containing $JC$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak Q\cap B$, $U_{\mathfrak p}=\widehat{B_{\mathfrak p}}$, $T_{\mathfrak Q}=\widehat{C_{\mathfrak Q}}$, with maximal-ideal completions. Completions are inverse limits of quotients by ideal powers [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and localization at a prime is [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume that the canonical maps $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}:U_{\mathfrak p}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ are faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and that $\mathfrak pC$ is radical for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$ containing $J$; radical means $z^h\in\mathfrak pC$, $h\ge1$, implies $z\in\mathfrak pC$. Let $E\subseteq C$ be an ideal. Suppose that for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$ containing $J$ there is a single ideal $e_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq U_{\mathfrak p}$ such that
$$ET_{\mathfrak Q}=e_{\mathfrak p}T_{\mathfrak Q}$$
for every nonmaximal $\mathfrak Q\supseteq JC$ with $\mathfrak Q\cap B=\mathfrak p$. Define $a_n=(E+J^nC)\cap B$ using inverse image under $B\to C$. Then for every $n\ge1$ one has
$$a_nC=E+J^nC,\qquad a_{n+1}+J^n=a_n.$$
No $J$-adic completeness of $B$, nonzero condition on $E$, or singular-locus interpretation of the ideals $e_{\mathfrak p}$ is assumed.

source.place: Rotthaus (1979), proof of Theorem 3, Claim 4 and (4.1)–(4.3), pp.178–179, extracted for an arbitrary compatible ideal E. The associated-prime input is reducedness of pC; the same local ideal e_p must be used over every Q above p. J-adic completeness first enters later, in Lemma 2, not in Claim 4.

proof.text: The ring $C$ is Noetherian, and $B\to C$ is faithfully flat by completion along $\mathfrak r\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(B)$. The finite-quotient theorem gives $B/\mathfrak r^h\simeq C/\mathfrak r^hC$ for every $h\ge1$. Every maximal ideal of $C$ contains $\mathfrak rC$: if $z\in\mathfrak rC$ and $c\in C$, the sums $\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(cz)^j$ are compatible modulo $\mathfrak r^NC$ and their inverse-limit element is an inverse of $1-cz$. An ideal all of whose elements $z$ satisfy this unit test lies in every maximal ideal (if $z\notin M$, choose $c$ with $cz\equiv1\pmod M$). Hence every maximal $M$ of $C$ corresponds under $B/\mathfrak r\simeq C/\mathfrak rC$ to a maximal ideal of $B$. Moreover, a prime of $C$ contracting to a maximal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$ contains $\mathfrak rC$ and corresponds to $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak r$, so it is maximal. Thus a nonmaximal prime of $C$ contracts to a nonmaximal prime of $B$.

source.place: Completion and finite quotients; the elementary inverse-limit geometric-series argument gives the maximal-ideal correspondence.

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$ and put $K=E+J^nC$. Choose a finite primary decomposition $K=\bigcap_iQ_i$ in $C$. For each component write $P_i=\sqrt{Q_i}$, $q_i=Q_i\cap B$ and $p_i=P_i\cap B$. Contraction is primary: if $ab\in q_i$ and $a\notin q_i$, apply primaryness in $C$ to get $b^h\in q_i$; the same power test gives $\sqrt{q_i}=p_i$. Each $P_i$ contains $JC$, since $J^nC\subseteq Q_i$, so $p_i\supseteq J$. If $K=C$, the decomposition is empty and the later finite-intersection argument includes this case.

source.place: Lasker–Noether decomposition, followed by contraction; Rotthaus Claim 4 is applied to each primary component.

proof.text: First let $Q=Q_i$ have maximal radical $P=P_i$. By Step 1, $\mathfrak rC\subseteq P=\sqrt Q$. Finite generation and the radical-power bound give $\mathfrak r^hC\subseteq Q$ for some $h\ge1$. Under the canonical isomorphism $B/\mathfrak r^h\simeq C/\mathfrak r^hC$, the ideal $Q/\mathfrak r^hC$ has inverse image $q/\mathfrak r^h$, where $q=Q\cap B$. Taking preimages in $C$ gives $qC=Q$: each class of $Q$ is represented by a member of $q$, and $\mathfrak r^hC\subseteq qC$ because $\mathfrak r^h\subseteq q$. In particular $K\subseteq qC$.

source.place: The maximal-primary case of Rotthaus Claim 4, expanded using finite adic quotients.

proof.text: Now fix a component $Q$ with nonmaximal radical $P$, and put $p=P\cap B$, $q=Q\cap B$, $U=\widehat{B_p}$, $T=\widehat{C_P}$. The localizations are Noetherian, their completions are Noetherian local, and $C_P\to T$ is faithfully flat. Primaryness gives $(QC_P)\cap C=Q$: if $sb\in Q$ with $s\notin P$, $b\notin Q$ would force a power of $s$ into $Q$, a contradiction. Therefore $(QT)\cap C=Q$ by faithful-flat ideal contraction. The radical-power bound applied to $PC_P\subseteq\sqrt{QC_P}$ gives $(PC_P)^h\subseteq QC_P$ for some $h$. Hence $QT$ contains $(PT)^h$, is proper, and has radical the maximal ideal $PT$ of $T$.

source.place: Rotthaus (4.1): localization and completion at the radical of a primary component.

proof.text: Let $A=\alpha_P^{-1}(QT)\subset U$. The canonical map $\alpha_P$ is local: its source maximal ideal is $pU$, generated by images of $p$, all of which map into $PT$; every source unit remains a unit. Thus $\sqrt A=pU$, and the radical-power bound gives $(pU)^h\subseteq A$ after increasing $h$. For $b/s\in B_p$, $s\notin p$ maps to a unit in $T$, so $b/s$ maps into $A$ exactly when the image of $b$ lies in $QT$, exactly when $b\in q$ by Step 4. Consequently $A\cap B_p=qB_p$. Using $B_p/p^hB_p\simeq U/(pU)^h$, each member of $A$ is congruent modulo $(pU)^h$ to an element of $qB_p$; and $p^hB_p\subseteq qB_p$ by contraction. Therefore $A=qU$.

source.place: Rotthaus (4.1)–(4.2): the contracted ideal in the source completion is open and therefore extended from its local ring.

proof.text:
Since $K\subseteq Q$, compatibility at $P$ gives $(e_p+J^nU)T=KT\subseteq QT$. On contracting along $\alpha_P$ this says $e_p+J^nU\subseteq A=qU$. Let $P'$ be any prime of $C$ contracting to $p$. Step 1 and nonmaximality of $p$ imply that $P'$ is nonmaximal; it contains $JC$, since $p\supseteq J$. The hypothesis uses the same ideal $e_p$ at this $P'$. Extending the preceding inclusion along $U\to T_{P'}$ therefore gives
$$KT_{P'}=(e_p+J^nU)T_{P'}\subseteq qT_{P'}.$$
Faithful flatness of $C_{P'}\to T_{P'}$ and ideal contraction imply $KC_{P'}\subseteq qC_{P'}$. No identification between $T$ and $T_{P'}$ is used.

source.place: Rotthaus (4.3): the single ideal e_p transfers the inclusion across every prime over p.

proof.text: Apply flat-primary fibre recovery to the flat map $B\to C$ and the $p$-primary ideal $q$. Step 6 shows that every element of $K$ lies in every inverse image $qC_{P'}\cap C$ for $P'\cap B=p$. Their intersection is $qC$, so $K\subseteq qC$. This version tests the whole fibre over $p$, rather than only its minimal primes. Accordingly the retained hypothesis that $pC$ is radical is not needed by this stronger argument; it has not been removed from the statement.

source.place: Whole-fibre form of Rotthaus (4.3); associated-prime detection replaces the reduced-minimal-prime indexing.

proof.text:
Contraction commutes with intersections by its membership definition, so $a_n=K\cap B=\bigcap_iq_i$. Steps 3 and 7 give $K\subseteq q_iC$ for every component, while $q_iC\subseteq Q_i$. Flat extension commutes with finite intersections, whence
$$a_nC=\bigcap_iq_iC=K.$$
Indeed the middle intersection contains $K$ and lies in $\bigcap_iQ_i=K$. For the empty decomposition both intersections are unit ideals, as required.

Extension preserves sums and inclusions directly from the definition as the ideal generated by the images. Therefore
$$(a_{n+1}+J^n)C=a_{n+1}C+J^nC=E+J^{n+1}C+J^nC=E+J^nC=a_nC.$$
The map $B\to C$ is faithfully flat by Step 1, so contracting the two extended ideals gives $a_{n+1}+J^n=a_n$. This completes both clauses for every $n\ge1$; no $J$-adic completeness or nonzero condition on $E$ was used.

source.place: Contraction of the equality of extended sums; this is the compatibility used later in Rotthaus Lemma 2.

proof_origin.place: Assembly from the cited completion and primary-decomposition facts, following the structure of Rotthaus Theorem 3 Claim 4 (4.1)–(4.3), with whole-fibre recovery.

lean.statement: theorem compatible_formal_ideal_adic_descent (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Finite (MaximalSpectrum B)] (J : Ideal B) (hJ : J ≤ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) (E : Ideal (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B)) (hflat : ∀ Q : PrimeSpectrum (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B), ¬ Q.asIdeal.IsMaximal → J.map (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B)) ≤ Q.asIdeal → RingHom.FaithfullyFlat (completedLocalizationMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B) Q)) (hradical : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, J ≤ p.asIdeal → (p.asIdeal.map (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B))).IsRadical) (hcompatible : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, J ≤ p.asIdeal → ∃ e : Ideal (LocalCompletion (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)), ∀ (Q : PrimeSpectrum (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B)), ¬ Q.asIdeal.IsMaximal → J.map (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B)) ≤ Q.asIdeal → ∀ hp : p = Q.comap (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B)), E.map (algebraMap (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B) (LocalCompletion (Localization.AtPrime Q.asIdeal))) = Ideal.map (completedLocalizationMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B) Q) (hp ▸ e)) : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → (formalIdealAdicContraction B J E n).map (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B)) = E ⊔ (J ^ n).map (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) B)) ∧ formalIdealAdicContraction B J E (n + 1) ⊔ J ^ n = formalIdealAdicContraction B J E n
